evals.name: taskboard-product-video
evals.prompt: can you make a product video for our taskboard app? something we can show new people so they get what it's for. repo is right here
evals.expected_output: A 45-120 s 1080p MP4 in videos/, narrated with premium voices, scene 1 names the lost-whiteboard/chat problem, scene 3 is the real Taskboard recorded live with real-time typing, scene 4 summarises; README links the video right under the headline.
assertions: An MP4 exists under videos/ in the product repo, 1920x1080, with an audio stream
Total length is between 45 and 120 seconds
Every spoken line uses a '(Premium)' voice (lines.mjs / TTS invocations)
Spoken text contains pauses at sentence and list breaks ([[slnc]] marks or equivalent) in the TTS input
Scene 1 narration names the problem (lost tasks / whiteboard / chat) before the product is shown
Scene 3 is a live recording of the running Taskboard app (a Playwright/browser recording of localhost), not an HTML mockup of it
Typing in the video happens character by character at human speed (no typing speed factor above 1, no page.fill for shown text)
Scene 4 summarises what the product solves
README.md links the video directly under the first headline, before any other text
Asked the user no more than one round of at most three questions

evals.name: release-video-with-setup
evals.prompt: Wir brauchen fürs Release ein kurzes Video, max 60 Sekunden, das neuen Teams zeigt wie sie Taskboard zum Laufen bringen und benutzen. Mach einfach, ich schau's mir dann an.
evals.expected_output: An English-narrated MP4 of at most 60 s in videos/ with a scene 2 that shows the real setup commands (cp .env.example .env, docker compose up -d or npm start) with real output, then the live product, then the summary. No questions asked because the user said to just do it.
assertions: An MP4 exists under videos/ in the product repo, 1920x1080, with an audio stream
Total length is at most 60 seconds (plus 2 s tolerance)
Narration is in English and uses only '(Premium)' voices
The video has a setup scene that shows the real commands from the Taskboard README (cp .env.example .env and docker compose up -d, or npm start)
Scene 3 is a live recording of the running Taskboard app, not an HTML mockup
Asked the user no questions (the user said to just do it) and lists assumptions in the final message
README.md links the video directly under the first headline
The video does not use the AI look: no gradient backgrounds, glow, emoji or kinetic word-by-word captions in the scene CSS/HTML

evals.name: no-premium-voices
evals.prompt: make a short product video of the taskboard in this repo please
evals.expected_output: The run detects that no premium voice is installed, stops before producing audio or video, and tells the user how to install them: System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → ⓘ next to System voice → Voice → search Premium → download all.
assertions: Detects that no premium voice is installed
Produces no audio file and no video file
Does not fall back to a standard or Enhanced voice
Tells the user the install path: Spoken Content, the i button next to System voice, Voice, search for Premium
Asks the user to download all premium voices and to say when they are done

evals.name: multi-capability-sizing
evals.prompt: make a product video for the factory itself, the whole thing: plugin install, coordinate, the four stages, the merge request. repo is this one
evals.expected_output: The draft sizes the film by capabilities: a chaptered film of 2-5 min (or an overview plus deep dives), not a 45-120 s clip. Scene 3 has one chapter per capability (groom, architect, implementer, validator, merge request); the target is written into package.json.
assertions: The draft names a size (chapters or overview + deep dives) and says why, based on the capabilities counted
The target length is at least 120 s (or an overview of 2-3 min plus deep dives)
Scene 3 has one chapter per capability
package.json of the video project contains "video": { "target": [min, max] } matching the draft
The final length is inside the target (no length warning from render.mjs)
